column1: # Version-control conflict markers (issue #5).
# None of `<`, `=` or `>` is an aontu operator, so a marker line was
# ordinary text once: `<<<<<<< HEAD` parsed happily into the two-string
# list ["<<<<<<<","HEAD"] and an unresolved merge became a plausible
# DOCUMENT rather than an error. Since 0.58.0 the bare-text rule refuses
# such a run anyway (op-chars.tsv), but with a code that says nothing
# about merges. A file in that state is never what the author meant, so
# it is refused before the parse, with a code of its own.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect ; modes: errc|err|gens
# All three marker lines, alone and in the shape git actually leaves.
conflict-open
conflict-sep
conflict-close
conflict-whole
# The marker is reported wherever it sits, not only on line one.
conflict-later-line
conflict-msg
# ... and what must NOT be refused AS A CONFLICT. The run length and
# the line start are both load-bearing: a document may legitimately hold
# these characters, and refusing one that does as a merge would be a
# worse bug than the one being fixed. Each row below is a shape that
# LOOKS like a marker somewhere. Quoted, it is a string. Bare, it is
# refused too -- by the bare-text rule, `<` and `=` being punctuation
# outside any syntax -- but with THAT code, never this one.
conflict-not-quoted-open
conflict-not-quoted-sep
conflict-not-inside-string
# Six is not seven, and eight is not seven.
conflict-not-six
conflict-not-eight
# A marker must start the LINE: indented, it is a run of text again --
# one the bare-text rule refuses.
conflict-not-indented
# Seven followed by something other than a space is not the git shape.
conflict-not-glued
